answers.topic: Tiered Pricing: the page trail (breadcrumbs) at the top of a tier's page and a matrix's page
answers.question:
Where should the page trail start?
(a) At Settings, as the PRD writes it: Settings › Pricing › Tiers › [tier name], and Settings › Pricing › Matrices › [matrix name] (suggested: it is the PRD's text and shows the way back to Settings)
(b) At Pricing, as the design draws it: Pricing › Tiers › [tier name]
(c) Something else (please say).
answers.what_we_knew: The PRD writes the trail from Settings. Every design picture of these pages starts it at "Pricing ›". Everything else on these pages is tested now; only the first part of the trail waits.
answers.where_found: PRD Story 2 (a tier's page) and Story 3 (a matrix's page); Tiered Pricing design canvas, pictures 2.11, 2.32, 2.46, 3.2, 4.26
answers.answer_verbatim: (b) Start at Pricing, as the design draws it: Pricing › Tiers › [tier name] and Pricing › Matrices › [matrix name]. A Settings crumb would need a page to return to. The Settings side panel is always visible, so no one needs to go back to a Settings page to start over. Clicking a Settings crumb would open the Settings section of Settings, which defaults to the Organization settings page, and we don't want that. PRD fix needed: remove "Settings ›" from S2-R28, S3-R26 and S7-R6.
answers.read: 2026-11-16T12:51Z (Google Sheets get_values, Sheet1!A1:H40, column E rows 6-36)

answers.topic: Tiered Pricing: the Delete [tier]? window
answers.question:
Should the window add the line "This can't be undone."?
(a) No: it asks "Delete [tier]?" with only "Parts already on work orders keep their prices.", as the PRD writes (suggested)
(b) Yes: add "This can't be undone.", as the design draws
(c) Something else (please say).
answers.what_we_knew: The PRD says the question is just "Delete [tier]?" with the line "Parts already on work orders keep their prices." The design's window adds "This can't be undone." The rest of deleting a tier is tested now.
answers.where_found: PRD Story 2 (deleting a tier); Tiered Pricing design canvas, picture 2.29
answers.answer_verbatim: (c) Delete [tier]? drops "Parts already on work orders keep their prices." and says "This can't be undone." instead. A tier can only be deleted when it never priced a saved line and no open work order, estimate or Part Sale keeps it (S2-R8, S2-R13), so the parts line doesn't apply to Delete. Archive keeps the parts line. Any "These tiers price the same as…" list stays on both. PRD fix needed: S2-R30 and the messages table (Delete wording separate from Archive).

answers.topic: Tiered Pricing: moving a category to a matrix from the matrix's page
answers.question:
On an existing matrix's page, when does a category picked on the Categories line move to that matrix (so its parts start pricing by it)?
(a) As soon as the picker closes, as the developers built it (suggested: the PRD also says category changes save without asking, apart from the grid)
(b) Only when the user clicks Save on the matrix
(c) Something else (please say).
answers.what_we_knew: The PRD says a category picked there "moves it to this matrix when the matrix is saved", and also that renaming and changing its categories save without asking. The developers' plan moves it when the picker closes (on a new matrix, with Create Matrix). The design has no picture of this on an existing matrix. Moving a category changes the price of every part in it, so the tester must know when to expect it.
answers.where_found: PRD Story 3 (the matrix page's Categories line); developers' plan for Tiered Pricing (11 Nov 2026), the Categories picker decision
answers.answer_verbatim: (b) The category is saved in the picker when picked, like our normal dropdown pickers, but its parts don't start pricing by this matrix until the whole matrix is saved with Save. The Categories picker works only in Edit, so Save always covers it (on a new matrix, Create Matrix). PRD S3-R13 already says "when the matrix is saved"; PRD fix needed: say the Categories line can be changed only in Edit. The developers' build (moves on picker close) changes.

answers.topic: Tiered Pricing: the change count in the grid's edit bar
answers.question:
After a column's rule type is changed on a 3-range matrix (and nothing else), how many changes should the edit bar count?
(a) 1: the column whose rule type differs counts as one change (suggested)
(b) 3: one per changed box, as the design draws
(c) Something else (please say).
answers.what_we_knew: The PRD counts "each column whose rule type differs" as one change, but also counts each changed box. The design shows "3 changes" for one type change on a 3-range column.
answers.where_found: PRD Story 4 (the edit bar); Tiered Pricing design canvas, picture 4.11
answers.answer_verbatim: (c) The rule-type change counts as 1, and each box whose value changes counts as 1 more. A 3-range column switched to % Off shows "1 change" (boxes start empty, question 13); after a value is typed in each box it shows "4 changes". After Save, the Audit Log records both: 1 rule type changed and 3 range values changed. Reason (Matt): every action must be recorded for audit, so a column quietly changed from 15% margin to a large % off is fully traceable. PRD fix needed: S4-R4 counting and the Audit Log wording (Story 4 / S19-R19) to state this example.

answers.topic: Tiered Pricing: the message after saving a matrix grid
answers.question:
Which form should the save message take?
(a) The PRD's form, for example "1 change: Tier 5 is 28% margin." (suggested)
(b) The design's form with the range, for example "1 change: Tier 2 $0.00–$100.00: 22% margin."
(c) Something else (please say).
answers.what_we_knew: The PRD's example names the tier and the new rule. The design's message also names the cost range.
answers.where_found: PRD Story 4 (saving the grid); Tiered Pricing design canvas, picture 3.12
answers.answer_verbatim: (c) It depends on what changed, per tier: • One rule and value across every range of the tier: the PRD's form, "1 change: Tier 5 is 28% margin." • The same rule type with a different value in each range: "Tier 5 is" followed by a bullet list of each range's rule, for example "• $0.00 to $25.00: 35% margin • $25.01 to $100.00: 28% margin". • More than one rule type in the tier: "Tier 5 is multiple rules" followed by a bullet list of the types, for example "• + $ • Margin %". The toast's "up to three changes, then and <n> more" rule (S4-R12) still applies; each tier is one item. PRD fix needed: S4-R12 and the messages table get these three forms. Canvas 3.12 and the build follow.

answers.topic: Tiered Pricing: parts added to a paid work order that is reopened
answers.question:
When a paid work order is reopened by adding a line, which tier prices the parts added to it?
(a) The customer's tier as it is now, as the developers built it (suggested: the new parts are new work done after payment, the same way a split work order takes the customer's current tier)
(b) The tier the work order was made with, as the PRD's general rule would say
(c) Something else (please say).
answers.what_we_knew: The PRD says a work order keeps the tier its customer had when it was made; moving a customer to another tier affects only work orders made afterwards or by splitting. No sentence covers reopening. The developers built the reopened work order to take the customer's current tier and told Product as an FYI. It decides the price on a real invoice for any customer whose tier changed since the job was opened.

answers.answer_verbatim: (a) The customer's tier as it is now, as the developers built it. Code check (Nov 16): adding a line to a work order whose invoice is Sent or Paid doesn't reopen it; it creates a new linked work order (new number, Approved) and the paid one and its invoice are untouched (CreateCommandHandler.php, PayedWorkOrderReopenedSubscriber.php). So the new work order takes the customer's current tier, as any new work order does. PRD fix needed: Story 10 adds this case (a line added to a paid work order goes on a new work order, priced by the customer's current tier).

answers.what_we_knew: Comparing the design's pictures of the same screen: the Price Part Simulator's columns move between view and edit (Part Cost about 70 pixels wider in edit); on New Matrix, opening the categories list pushes the tabs and grid down about 221 pixels; on Manage Customers the tier columns move left 11 to 83 pixels when a search narrows the list; on Sales by Tier the number columns move 58 to 94 pixels when a row or a customer is opened and 20 to 36 pixels on the empty states; on Sales by Category they move 5 to 10 pixels when a category is opened; the report filter chips shift as a picked chip widens; on a work order the lines table's columns move 19 to 71 pixels while the Add Part row is open and 1 to 9 pixels after a part is added or received.
